posts.text: Copper has hit $14,533/tonne, up 16% this year — The price isn’t the only thing worth watching. SHFE copper inventories have fallen about 85% from their March peak to around 63,000 tonnes. That’s a sharp drawdown. With mine supply also facing disruptions, the concern is shifting from demand to how much readily available copper is actually left. For Indian stocks, higher copper prices have two sides. Copper producers benefit from higher realisations. Wire, cable and electrical equipment makers have to deal with higher input costs. So I wouldn’t look at copper’s rally as a blanket positive for m…
